n24a30ffc89b.s: In seawater, the extra hydrogen ions released by carbonic acid bind with:
n24a30ffc89b.x: Extra H+ ions bind carbonate ions, so less carbonate is left for shells and skeletons.

n45344049e4a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about coral reef monitoring in India?
o: NCCR, Chennai monitors reef health through D-COIN
Coral bleaching alerts through the SAMUDRA app are issued by NCCR, Chennai
The SAMUDRA app is run by INCOIS
n45344049e4a.x: SAMUDRA app coral bleaching alerts come from INCOIS, not NCCR; NCCR, Chennai monitors reef health through D-COIN.

n6f914926729.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pavona clavus colony – Gulf of Kutch
n6f914926729.x: Lakshadweep is made up entirely of atoll reefs; the giant Pavona clavus colony is at Kadmat in Lakshadweep.

ndc9044fc05e.s: Each 1°C rise in temperature lets the atmosphere hold about ____ more moisture.
ndc9044fc05e.x: Warmer air holds about 7% more moisture per 1°C, which intensifies extreme rainfall and flash floods. (No dates for a sequence, so a one-liner.)

ne9b3a218c6e.s: The World Meteorological Organization, set up in 1950, became a UN specialised agency in:
ne9b3a218c6e.x: WMO was set up in 1950 and became a UN specialised agency in 1951; its headquarters is at Geneva.

n2aee034f91d.s: Permafrost thaw in the Himalaya releases:
n2aee034f91d.x: Permafrost thaw releases CH4 and CO2 and can damage infrastructure.

na22b1bd7d85.s: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the WMO State of the Global Climate 2025?
o: Global sea level has risen about 11 cm since 1993
Oceans hold over 90% of the excess heat
Arctic sea ice is near a record low
Glacier loss threatens the water supply of about 200 million people
na22b1bd7d85.x: Glacier loss threatens water for about 2 billion people, not 200 million.

n4936df21912.s: At 1.5°C of warming, an ice-free Arctic summer is projected about:
n4936df21912.x: At 1.5°C an ice-free Arctic summer is projected once a century; once a decade applies at 2°C.

n278f391b55c.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Joint Implementation – Projects in developing countries
n278f391b55c.x: CDM yields CERs from projects in developing countries; Joint Implementation yields ERUs from projects in other Annex I countries.

nd75acb83504.s: Under the NCQG agreed at COP29, the call to reach US$1.3 trillion a year from all sources is:
o: Binding only on Annex II countries
nd75acb83504.x: The US$1.3 trillion call is non-binding; the core goal is US$300 billion a year by 2035.

n91b7bb8848d.s: How many voluntary indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation were adopted at COP30, Belém?
n91b7bb8848d.x: COP30 adopted 59 voluntary GGA indicators and an adaptation finance target of US$120 billion a year.

n838e066da2f.s: The Adaptation Fund is financed by what share of proceeds from CDM Certified Emission Reductions?
n838e066da2f.x: The Adaptation Fund gets a 2 per cent share of CDM CER proceeds.

nfaf2179e220.s: India has hosted the Voice of Global South Summits since:
nfaf2179e220.x: India has hosted the summits since January 2023 to press developing-country finance and technology needs; they are not a CBAM mechanism. (No dated series for a sequence, so a one-liner.)

n262384a74a4.s: The first COP decision calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems was the:
n262384a74a4.x: The UAE Consensus at COP28 was the first COP decision on transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems.

n8cc1e059d31.s: Which of the following is listed among India's coal-related mitigation measures?
n8cc1e059d31.x: India's coal measures include coal washing, ESPs, gasification, wet scrubbers, low-NOx burners and CCS/CCUS; ocean fertilisation is not among them.

nenvironment-8-10.x: COP28 (2023) was held at Dubai; Sharm el-Sheikh hosted COP27 and Baku the finance COP29.

nc7329d27c7f.s: The Green Climate Fund is headquartered at:
nc7329d27c7f.x: The GCF is headquartered at Songdo, Incheon (South Korea), not Washington, D.C.

n6526317d69d.s: The European Green Deal aims to make the EU net-zero in greenhouse gas emissions by:
n6526317d69d.x: The European Green Deal targets net zero by 2050; Farm to Fork is one of its components.

n65013e08b68.x: The Montreal Protocol deals with ozone-depleting substances; hazardous waste is the Basel Convention's subject.

o: Prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides
nenvironment-16-2.x: Rotterdam covers prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides; biosafety and GMOs come under the Cartagena Protocol.

new.s: The primary cause of ocean acidification is:
o: Acid rain falling on the sea
Dissolution of atmospheric CO2 in seawater
new.x: Ocean acidification is caused mainly by atmospheric CO2 dissolving in seawater (APPSC-GS 2024), not by acid rain.

new.s: Oceans absorb about what share of the CO2 released by human activities?
new.x: Oceans take up about one-third of human CO2 (also cited as 30-40%).

new.s: Despite acidification, the surface ocean today is:
new.x: pH has fallen only from about 8.2 to 8.1, so the ocean is still alkaline even though acidity has risen about 30%.

new.s: The symbiotic algae that give reef-building corals food and colour are called:
new.x: Zooxanthellae live in coral tissue and supply food and colour; corals lose them when heat-stressed.

new.s: The skeletons of reef-building corals are made of:
new.x: Reef-building corals secrete calcium carbonate skeletons.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about coral bleaching:
1. Heat-stressed corals lose their zooxanthellae.
2. The 4th global bleaching event was declared by UNEP in 2024.
3. Earlier global bleaching events occurred in 1998, 2010 and 2014-17.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The 4th global bleaching event was declared by NOAA-ICRI in April 2024, not UNEP.

new.s: The 4th global coral bleaching event (2023-25) affected about what share of the world's reefs?
new.x: The 4th global bleaching event hit about 84% of the world's reefs in 82 countries and territories.

new.s: Which Indian reef area has the most diverse reefs in India?
new.x: Andaman and Nicobar reefs are the most diverse in India; the Gulf of Kutch reefs are among the world's most northerly.

new.s: Corals and bivalve larvae are more sensitive to acidification because their shells and skeletons use:
new.x: Aragonite is more soluble than calcite, so organisms using it are hit harder.

new.s: Pteropods matter for fisheries under ocean acidification mainly because they are:
new.x: Pteropods (sea butterflies) are a key food for fish, and their shells dissolve as the sea acidifies.

new.s: A marine heatwave is defined as sea-surface temperature 3-4°C above average for at least:
new.x: A marine heatwave means SST 3-4°C above average for at least 5 days.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of coral restoration method and site is correctly matched?
new.x: Coral translocation is used for the Great Nicobar project; Biorock is in the Gulf of Kutch and 3D-printed reefs off Ramanathapuram.

new.s: Biorock technology was invented in 1976 by:
new.x: Biorock (mineral accretion) was invented in 1976 by Wolf Hilbertz.

new.s: The indicator for SDG target 14.3 on ocean acidification is:
new.x: SDG 14.3 aims to minimise ocean acidification, measured by average marine pH.

new.s: Matsya 6000, under India's Deep Ocean Mission, is a:
new.x: Matsya 6000 is the 3-member submersible of Samudrayaan; Varaha is the deep-sea mining system.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the IMD Statement on Climate of India:
1. 2019 was the 7th warmest year since 1901.
2. 2024 was the warmest year since 1901.
3. 2025 was the 2nd warmest year since 1901.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: 2019 was the 7th warmest and 2024 the warmest year since 1901; 2025 was the 8th warmest, not 2nd.

new.s: In 2019, the 7th warmest year since 1901, which state suffered most from extreme weather according to IMD?
new.x: IMD named Bihar as the state that suffered most in 2019 (APPSC 2018 key).

new.s: India warmed by about how much over 1901-2018?
new.x: India warmed about 0.7°C over 1901-2018, not more than 2°C.

new.s: The hottest place in Andhra Pradesh, Rentachintala, is in which district?
new.x: Rentachintala in Palnadu district is AP's hottest place.

new.s: Between 1981 and 2020, extreme pre-monsoon rain events in India have:
new.x: Extreme pre-monsoon rain events doubled over 1981-2020.

new.s: The north-east monsoon (October-December) gives about what share of India's annual rainfall?
new.x: The NE monsoon gives about 11%, while the SW monsoon gives about 75%.

new.s: The Climate-Smart Village approach is promoted under the CCAFS programme of:
new.x: Climate-Smart Village comes under CCAFS of CGIAR; NICRA is the ICAR/CRIDA project.

new.s: How many climate-resilient crop varieties were released in India during 2014-2025?
new.x: 2,996 climate-resilient varieties were released in 2014-2025, including heat-tolerant wheat HD 3385.

new.s: According to FAO-WMO (April 2026), extreme heat cuts milk yield by about:
new.x: Extreme heat cuts milk yield by 15-25%; heat stress sets in above 25°C.

new.s: NICRA, led by CRIDA, Hyderabad, was launched by ICAR in:
new.x: NICRA is an ICAR project of 2011, led by CRIDA, Hyderabad.

new.s: The South Lhonak lake GLOF of October 2023 occurred in:
new.x: South Lhonak is in Sikkim; the Chamoli disaster (Feb 2021) was in Uttarakhand.

new.s: ICIMOD, which publishes the Hindu Kush Himalaya Snow Update, is headquartered at:
new.x: ICIMOD is based in Kathmandu; its 2025 Snow Update found snow persistence 23.6% below normal.

new.s: The Gangotri glacier has retreated by about how much since 1935?
new.x: Gangotri has retreated about 1,727 m since 1935, faster in recent years.

new.s: INCOIS prepares Coastal Vulnerability Index maps using how many parameters?
new.x: INCOIS, Hyderabad, builds Coastal Vulnerability Index maps from 7 parameters.

new.s: Which of the following is a shoreline erosion hotspot on the Andhra Pradesh coast?
new.x: Uppada (Kakinada) and the Krishna coast are AP's erosion hotspots.

new.s: Between 2001 and 2019, the number of cyclones over the Arabian Sea rose by about:
new.x: Arabian Sea cyclones rose 52%; very severe cyclones rose 150%.

new.s: According to NCCR, Chennai, about what share of India's coastline was eroding during 1990-2018?
new.x: NCCR, Chennai found 33.6% of India's coastline eroding over 1990-2018.

new.s: In 2025, marine heatwaves affected roughly what share of the world's oceans?
new.x: Over 90% of oceans saw marine heatwaves in 2025, lowering oxygen and harming fish.

new.s: Which of the following was among the most vulnerable states in the DST (2021) climate vulnerability assessment?
new.x: DST (2021) listed Jharkhand, Mizoram, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh and West Bengal.

new.s: In the Climate Risk Index 2021 (16th edition), India was ranked:
new.x: CRI 2021 ranked India 7th; CRI 2026 ranked it 9th over 1995-2024.

new.s: Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea, islets that went under the sea in 1999, belong to:
new.x: Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea were Kiribati islets lost in 1999.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about adaptation measures in India?
o: PMFBY crop insurance was launched in 2016
Mangroves and Casuarina act as bio-shields on the AP coast
CWC issues flood forecasts at 3,500 stations
The NDC 2031-35 includes adaptation for coasts and heat
new.x: CWC issues flood forecasts at 350 stations, not 3,500.

new.s: The Central Water Commission issues flood forecasts at about how many stations?
new.x: CWC flood forecasting covers 350 stations, a frequent trap with 3,500.

new.s: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, an adaptation measure for farmers, was launched in:
new.x: PMFBY, India's crop insurance scheme, was launched in 2016.

new.s: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 at:
new.x: The UNFCCC was adopted in New York and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992.

new.s: The UNFCCC Secretariat is located at:
new.x: The UNFCCC Secretariat is at Bonn; the IPCC Secretariat is at Geneva.

new.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the CBDR-RC principle is correctly matched?
new.x: CBDR-RC appears in Rio Principle 7, UNFCCC Article 3.1 and Paris Agreement Article 2.2.

new.s: The second commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol (2013-2020) was set by the:
new.x: The Doha Amendment (2012) set the second period with an 18% cut below 1990; it entered into force on 31 December 2020.

new.s: Under the Doha Amendment, the second Kyoto commitment period required a cut of ____ below 1990 levels.
new.x: The second period (2013-2020) required an 18% cut below 1990; the first required about 5%.

new.s: One carbon credit is equal to:
new.x: One carbon credit equals one tonne of CO2 equivalent emitted, reduced or removed.

new.s: Certified Emission Reductions (CERs) are issued by the:
new.x: CERs are issued by the CDM Executive Board, not under the Nagoya Protocol.

new.s: The emission targets in the NDCs under the Paris Agreement are legally binding on:
new.x: No party is bound to its NDC target; only the procedural duties to prepare, communicate and report NDCs are binding (APPSC-G2 2025).

new.s: Under Article 13 of the Paris Agreement, the first Biennial Transparency Reports were due by the end of:
new.x: Article 13 set up the Enhanced Transparency Framework; first Biennial Transparency Reports were due by end-2024.

new.s: The Global Stocktake under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement takes place every:
new.x: The Global Stocktake is held every 5 years; the first concluded at COP28.

new.s: In India's updated NDC of 2022, the emissions-intensity reduction target (from 2005 levels) by 2030 is:
new.x: The 2022 update set 45% by 2030; the INDC had 33-35% and the 2031-35 NDC sets 47% by 2035.

new.s: COP31 in 2026 is hosted at:
new.x: COP31 (2026) is at Antalya, Türkiye; COP32 (2027) is at Addis Ababa.

new.s: Which of the following COP-host pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: COP24 was at Katowice; COP23 was at Bonn, COP25 at Madrid and COP16 at Cancun.

new.s: The only COP hosted by India was:
new.x: COP8 at New Delhi in 2002 is the only COP held in India; it adopted the Delhi Ministerial Declaration.

new.s: The Mitigation Work Programme, with at least two global dialogues a year to 2030, was agreed at:
new.x: COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh set up the Mitigation Work Programme and reaffirmed the 1.5°C pursuit.

new.s: At COP28, countries agreed by 2030 to triple renewable energy capacity to:
new.x: COP28 called for tripling renewables to 11,000 GW and doubling energy-efficiency gains to 4% a year by 2030.

new.s: Saraswathi of Malluvalasa, Vizianagaram, was featured at which event?
new.x: She was featured at Sustaina India 2025, a CEEW exhibition in New Delhi, not at a COP28 recognition.

new.s: The Global Shield against Climate Risks was launched at COP27 by:
new.x: The Global Shield was launched at COP27 by the G7 and V20 to give pre-arranged finance for climate disasters.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Global Environment Facility:
1. It was founded in 1991.
2. It is headquartered at Songdo, Incheon.
3. It finances the UNFCCC, CBD and Minamata Convention.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The GEF was founded in 1991, is headquartered at Washington DC and finances UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm and Minamata; Songdo is the GCF's HQ.

new.s: The Green Climate Fund was set up at:
new.x: The GCF was set up in 2010 at COP16, Cancun, not Durban.

new.s: The Climate Group, which runs RE100 and EV100, is a:
o: Non-profit set up in London in 2003
new.x: The Climate Group is a London non-profit founded in 2003 that runs RE100 and EV100.

new.s: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC), founded in 2012 by UNEP and six countries, targets:
new.x: CCAC (2012, UNEP plus six countries) works on short-lived climate pollutants.

new.s: The Global Methane Pledge seeks to cut methane emissions by 2030, from 2020 levels, by:
new.x: The Global Methane Pledge targets a 30% cut from 2020 levels by 2030; India is not a member.

new.s: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with:
new.x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

new.s: According to the IPCC SR1.5 (2018), warming is likely to reach 1.5°C between:
new.x: SR1.5 projected 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052, with net zero needed around 2050.

new.s: The AR6 Synthesis Report put warming over 2011-2020 at about:
new.x: AR6 SYR (2023) assessed warming at 1.1°C over 2011-2020, with emissions at their highest ever.

new.s: Which of the following IPCC special reports is correctly matched with its subject?
o: SRCCL – Land use, desertification and food security
new.x: SRCCL (Aug 2019) covers land use, desertification, degradation and food security; SROCC covers oceans and the cryosphere.

new.s: The IPCC SROCC (2019) found that marine heatwaves have become:
new.x: SROCC found marine heatwaves more frequent and oceans holding over 90% of excess heat.

new.s: In the IPCC Shared Socioeconomic Pathways, SSP3 is called:
new.x: SSP3 is Regional Rivalry; SSP1 is Sustainability and SSP5 Fossil-fuelled Development.

new.s: The IPCC AR7 cycle includes a Special Report, planned for 2027, on:
new.x: AR7, begun in July 2023, includes a Special Report on Climate Change and Cities planned for 2027.

new.s: IPCC Working Group II deals with:
new.x: WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability; WG I is physical science and WG III mitigation.

new.s: The BASIC group of countries in climate negotiations has how many members?
new.x: BASIC has four members; India attended its 19th meeting at Sun City.

new.s: In climate equity debates, the term 'carbon space' refers to:
o: Room for developing countries to grow
Forest area used as carbon sinks
Carbon budget left for developed countries
new.x: Carbon space means the room developing countries need to grow; historical responsibility points to developed countries' past emissions.

new.s: The Green Development Pact was adopted at the:
new.x: The G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 Sep 2023) adopted the Green Development Pact and launched the Global Biofuels Alliance.

new.s: Which of the following has India NOT signed?
o: Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use
new.x: India did not sign the Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use, nor the Global Methane Pledge; it ratified the Paris Agreement on 2 Oct 2016.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Deep Ocean Mission:
1. Samudrayaan is India's first manned deep ocean mission, targeting 6,000 m.
2. Varaha is the 3-member submersible of Samudrayaan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Samudrayaan is the first manned mission to 6,000 m; Matsya 6000 is the submersible, while Varaha is the deep-sea mining system tested at 5,270 m.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kyoto Protocol:
1. It set binding emission targets for Annex I countries only.
2. Canada was the first country to withdraw from it.
3. The USA ratified it in 2005.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Kyoto binds only Annex I countries and Canada was the first to leave (effective 2012); the USA never ratified it.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zanskar glacier study – Central Water Commission
new.x: Himansh, NCPOR's station of 2016, is in Lahaul-Spiti; Chamoli is in Uttarakhand, South Lhonak in Sikkim, and the Zanskar study was by IIT Bombay.

new.s: Which of the following conventions directly addresses greenhouse gases?
new.x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) phases down HFCs, a greenhouse gas; Basel, Minamata and Rotterdam do not address GHGs.
